name: Enflame S60 (SCORPIO-AO) AI accelerator
notes:
THE HIERARCHY POINT: this is the thinnest record in the slice and it is thin for a defensible reason: Enflame is one of the least transparent accelerator vendors in existence, its own website is behind a WAF that blocks automated access entirely, and the ONE authoritative independent source - a TechInsights teardown (cn-enflame-techinsights) - establishes the part's existence and process node but paywalls everything quantitative. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: the S60 is Enflame's THIRD-generation AI accelerator card; its compute chiplet carries 'ENFLAME SCORPIO-AO' die markings; it was manufactured by TSMC on N6NTO-HPC. That process_nm: 6 field is the only hard number in this record and it comes from an independent teardown rather than a press release, which makes it the most trustworthy Enflame datum available. WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED: memory type, capacity, bandwidth, compute throughput at any precision, TDP, and form factor are all None because no source states them. TechInsights' analysis does include die utilisation broken out for logic, I/O memory and analog, and manufacturing cost, but that content sits behind a paid platform subscription and could not be read. THE OLDER ENFLAME PARTS ARE WORSE AND ARE DELIBERATELY NOT RECORDED HERE: T20 (SuiSi 1.5, PCIe, ~300 W, 2021), T21 (SuiSi 2.0, OAM, 400 W, 2022, claimed 160 TFLOPS TF32 and a cluster of 8000+ cards at 1.3 EFLOPS peak single-precision), i10/i20 inference line, and S60 itself. An unofficial Chinese AI-accelerator wiki (cn-cn-ai-accelerator-wiki) does publish T21 numbers and - to its credit - explicitly labels its FP16, INT8, memory capacity and memory bandwidth entries as unpublished-and-speculated. Those figures are therefore NOT recorded as an accelerator record: recording a part whose every number the source itself marks as a guess would violate this repo's core rule, and a record with four None fields and a note saying 'not recorded because the only source marks its own figures as speculation' would be documentation of nothing. VENDOR CONTEXT worth keeping: Enflame was founded March 2018 by two ex-AMD engineers, is Tencent-backed, licensed Arteris FlexNoC in 2018 for its on-chip backbone, sells predominantly to state-owned enterprises and has cooperated with local governments on AI computing hubs (Wuxi), was reported in June 2024 as submitting downgraded designs to TSMC to comply with US restrictions, and IPO'd on the SSE STAR Market in September 2026 (ticker 688801). The S60's third-generation status plus a TSMC N6 node plus a 2026 IPO is genuinely notable given the sanctions constraints - it implies Enflame secured N6-class foundry access, which is a materially harder procurement problem than the 7 nm N+1/N+2 parts the 910 line uses.
MEMORY_BUS_WIDTH: STILL NULL, AND HERE IS PRECISELY WHAT WAS LOOKED FOR (2026-10-04). %s NO FIGURE WAS BACK-COMPUTED FROM BANDWIDTH. That is the standing rule for this field in this repo and it was applied to every null here rather than to a subset: a width derived by dividing a published aggregate bandwidth by an assumed or half-assumed per-pin rate is two inferences stacked on one number, and if either inference is wrong the record looks populated while being wrong. The correct state of this field is 'the vendor does not publish it', and the note above names the specific document that was read and found not to carry it, so a future pass does not have to re-establish that from scratch.
